plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-14 from the official Salem College 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (current edition, catoid=34), History Major (BA) program page (poid=916). Salem College publishes major requirements but no official semester sequence for this program (its Print Degree Planner is a blank worksheet), so the plan is collected in requirements_only form as a single block. The recorded total is the exact sum of the itemized requirements at their exercised values, as disclosed below; the program page prints no hour total. The full degree requirements, including the Salem Impact core (published separately in the same catalog), are not itemized here. Per-course credits are the Hour(s) values printed on each course's own official course detail page in the same catalog; the program page itself prints no per-course credits. Prerequisites naming courses outside this plan are disclosed in these notes and are not recorded as plan prerequisites. The program requires eleven courses, at least five of which must be taken at Salem (residency as printed): five required courses (HIST 103, HIST 104, HIST 105, HIST 106, HIST 310) and two courses from each of three regional blocks (United States History; European History; African, Asian, Latin American, Middle Eastern History), each block recorded as two choose-one slots. The recorded total (33) is 15 required hours plus six slots exercised at 3; a completion using HIST 211 (4 Hour(s), United States block, disclosed on those slots, not listed) totals 34, as printed. HIST 310's description states it is required of majors in their senior year and juniors may take it with permission of instructor. Cross-listings as printed, each course counted once under its HIST code: HIST 215 is cross-listed with REST 210, HIST 265 with POLI 265, and HIST 248 with HHMN 248. HIST 282's title is truncated as printed in the catalog ('Women Healing and Medicine in Early Amer') on the program page, the Courses of Instruction list and its course detail page; it is transcribed as printed and not completed. The program's printed substitution rule -- up to three political science courses may be substituted upon approval by the program director -- names no specific courses, so no substituted course is placed. No fixed course in this plan prints a prerequisite; HIST 211's printed prerequisite is disclosed on the United States slots.

courses.title: United States History Elective
courses.choice_note: Choose one course for this United States History slot; the program requires two courses from the United States History block, recorded as two slots. Options listed at the slot's exercised 3 credits, in the catalog's printed order. The remaining catalog option, HIST 211 Salem Archives: Research and the Public Good, is printed at 4 Hour(s) (prerequisite: HIST 103 or HIST 104 or HIST 105 or HIST 106) and is disclosed here, not listed as a fixed option; a completion using it totals 1 hour more than the recorded total. Per the program's printed note, each 200-level (or above) course may be counted toward only one regional grouping, so the courses taken for the two United States slots must be distinct and may not also serve another regional block.
